gold_assessment.reasoning: Gold: dysuria as chief complaint. Generated cc-001: 'pain when urinating' conveys dysuria, so concept is captured.

Gold: 6-day history of dysuria with burning, stinging sensation. Gen hpi-001: 6-day history of dysuria and foul-smelling urine. Duration and dysuria covered; burning/stinging quality is omitted, and 'foul-smelling' is an added descriptor.
Gold: no difficulty actually passing urine. Gen hpi-006: 'able to void urine' expresses same concept (no voiding difficulty).
Gold: strong odour to urine. Gen hpi-001: 'foul-smelling urine' captures this meaning.
Gold: blood in urine (haematuria). Gen hpi-003: 'hematuria described as spotting' covers presence of hematuria, with extra detail about spotting.
Gold: eating and drinking normally. Gen hpi-007: 'eating and drinking normally' matches.

Gold: denies any new per-vaginal discharge. Gen facts mention 'denies vaginal discharge' (ros-004) but do not specify 'new' or 'per-vaginal'; however, clinically this is essentially the same concept. Still, the nuance of 'new' is not explicitly present, so treated as partially represented but not exact; per instructions, small details matter, so mark as OMITTED.
Gold: denies back or loin pain. Gen hpi-005 and ros-002: 'denies loin or back pain' – same content.
Gold: central abdominal pain. Gen hpi-002: intermittent mid-abdominal pain rated 7/10. Location covered and additional details (intermittent, severity) added.
Gold: not feverish but has not checked temperature. Gen hpi-004/ros-001: 'denies fever'. This captures 'not feverish' but omits the detail that temperature has not been checked.
Gold: no obvious trigger and no history of dehydration or frequent sexual intercourse preceding symptoms. No generated fact addresses triggers, dehydration history, or sexual intercourse history.
Gold: no past history of urine infections or similar symptoms. No generated fact covers prior UTI/similar symptom history.
Gold: no recent change in bowel habits. No direct Gen statement, so actually not present. Therefore, this is OMITTED, not covered.
Gold: history of IBS. Gen pmh-001: same.
Gold: no relevant family history. Gen fh-001: 'no significant family illnesses' – equivalent meaning.

Gold: Mebeverine 200 mg TDS. Gen med-001: 'Mebavin 200 mg TID' – dose and frequency match, but drug name is slightly different (likely same agent, but not perfectly accurate). Also, Gen plan-006: continue Mebavin. Baseline med is substantially captured but with a naming discrepancy.
Gold: allergic to Clindamycin. Gen allergy-001: same.
Gold: lives with friends. Gen sh-001: 'lives with friends and works as a support worker' – includes living arrangement.
Gold: works as a support worker. Gen sh-001: includes 'support worker'.
Gold: non-smoker. Gen sh-003: non-smoker.
Gold: drinks ~1 unit/week. Gen sh-002: ~1 glass wine/week. Typical glass of wine approximates 1 alcohol unit, so alcohol intake is essentially captured but with unit wording difference.
Gold: likely UTI. Gen asm-001: probable uncomplicated lower UTI – equivalent assessment with extra 'uncomplicated, lower.'

Gold: specifically Nitrofurantoin 3-day course. Gen plan-001/med-002: 3-day oral antibiotic, unspecified drug. Duration and route covered, but drug name (Nitrofurantoin) is omitted; given clinical importance of exact agent, mark as OMITTED.
Gold: advised to keep well hydrated (no volume specified). Gen plan-002: encourage hydration 2.5–3 L/day. Same concept with additional quantitative detail.
Gold: cranberry juice may be beneficial. Gen plan-002: 'drink cranberry juice' as part of advice. Covered but without 'may' qualifier (stronger recommendation).
Gold: monitor temperature with a thermometer. Gen plan-004: buy thermometer and monitor temp. Same idea with added instruction to purchase the device.

Gold FU: contact clinic if fever, back pain, persistent symptoms, or recurrent episodes. Gen plan-005 (safety-net): seek review for increasing pain, fever, back/loin pain, urinary retention, or recurrent symptoms. All gold triggers except 'persistent symptoms' are clearly covered; 'recurrent episodes' matches 'recurrent symptoms.' Gen adds increasing pain and urinary retention. Missing explicit mention of persistent symptoms, so partially covered.

gen_assessment.reasoning: Pain when urinating is equivalent to dysuria in the gold chief complaint.

Six-day history of dysuria is supported. 'Foul-smelling urine' corresponds to strong odour (hpi-003). Combined, content is supported, but the generated fact omits the burning/stinging quality present in gold and merges two separate gold facts.
Gold only notes 'central abdominal pain' without severity or intermittency. 'Intermittent' and '7/10' severity are additional details not present in gold.
Hematuria is in gold. Describing it as 'spotting' is added detail but not contradictory.
Gold: patient not feverish but has not checked temperature. Generated 'denies fever' matches absence of fever but omits the nuance that temperature has not been measured.
Directly matches denial of loin/back pain.
Being able to void is equivalent to no difficulty actually passing urine.
Eating and drinking normally is explicitly in gold.
History of IBS present in both.
Dose and frequency (200 mg TID/TDS) match. However, the drug name 'Mebavin' differs from 'Mebeverine'; likely intended to be same but not exact, so only partially supported.

Gold specifies Nitrofurantoin 3-day course; generated fact: unspecified oral antibiotic 3-day course. Duration and antibiotic therapy are supported, but omission of the specific agent is a clinically relevant gap.
No mention of urine-alkalinising sachets in gold. Entirely new recommendation.
Allergy to Clindamycin matches exactly.
Both indicate no significant/relevant family history.
Living with friends and working as a support worker both appear in gold (sh-001 and sh-002).
Gold: ~1 unit/week. Generated: ~1 glass of wine/week. These are conceptually similar typical quantities, but unit terminology differs; overall partially supported.
Non-smoker is explicitly in gold.
Both describe likely/probable UTI; generated adds 'uncomplicated lower' but does not conflict.
Assessment of IBS as stable is not mentioned in gold; IBS appears only as past medical history, not as an assessment item.

Gold: Nitrofurantoin 3-day course. Generated: 3-day oral antibiotic course with e-script to a named pharmacy. Duration and that an antibiotic course is planned are supported; specific agent and pharmacy logistics are new/omitted details. Partially supported overall.

Hydration advice is supported by gold. The specific 2.5–3 L/day volume and inclusion of cranberry juice (overlaps with plan-003) are additional details; cranberry itself is supported by gold plan-003. Combined, this fact merges and extends gold items.
Urine-alkalinising sachets are not in the gold care plan; this is new advice.
Monitoring temperature with a thermometer is in gold; instruction to 'buy thermometer' is extra detail, so partially supported.

Gold FU: contact if fever, back pain, persistent symptoms, or recurrent episodes. Generated adds increasing pain and urinary retention; it omits explicit mention of 'persistent symptoms' but includes recurrent symptoms. Thus overlap is substantial but not complete.
Continuing Mebavin/Mebeverine for IBS is not mentioned in the gold plan; IBS med appears only as baseline medication, not a specific plan instruction.
Denial of fever is consistent with 'not feverish,' but the gold also specifies temperature has not been checked. Generated ROS lacks that nuance.
Denial of loin/back pain matches gold history.
Regular menses is not mentioned anywhere in gold facts.
Gold: 'no new per-vaginal discharge.' Generated: denies vaginal discharge. Core idea (no discharge) is similar, but gold specifies 'no new' and 'per-vaginal', so not an exact match.
